name: Password Sign-In Is Rejected
summary: The user submits password credentials that are not accepted, no session is established, and the client receives the same canonical rejected sign-in experience whether the internal cause is invalid credentials or an unknown account.

preconditions.expression: session-capability == anonymous and password credentials are submitted

inputs.name: Password
inputs.description: Submitted password. Runtime evidence covers both invalid-password and unknown-account rejection permutations without exposing account existence to the user.

serverInteraction.intent: Attempt password authentication and return a non-enumerating rejected result without establishing a session.

postconditions.expression: session-capability == anonymous and account-existence remains undisclosed and auth.sign-in.unable is visible

sourceReferences.note: PasswordSignInAsync distinguishes invalid credentials from user-not-found internally while leaving the caller unauthenticated.

InvalidCredentials_Should_ReturnFailure_And_RecordStartedThenFailed and UserNotFound_Should_ReturnFailure_And_RecordStartedThenUserNotFound provide two runtime proofs for this one canonical rejected scenario.
Canonical rejected surface offers retry, password recovery, email change, provider, and passkey alternatives without disclosing whether the submitted account exists.
Presentation review keeps Rejected on the generic auth.sign-in.unable surface and deliberately preserves the same user-visible outcome for invalid-password and unknown-account permutations.
